name: Glaetzer Shiraz Amon-Ra Barossa Valley 2012
text:
## Glaetzer Shiraz Amon-Ra Barossa Valley 2012

**The story.** The [Barossa Valley](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Barossa+Valley,+South+Australia,+Australia&t=k) is South Australia's wine heartland. Amon-Ra comes from the northern sub-region of [Ebenezer](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Ebenezer,+Barossa+Valley,+South+Australia,+Australia&t=k). The first Glaetzers settled in the Barossa in 1888, after emigrating from Brandenburg, Germany, and started in the town of Nuriootpa. The town is at [Nuriootpa](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Nuriootpa,+South+Australia,+Australia&t=k).

Ben Glaetzer founded Glaetzer Wines in 1995 at age 23, after training with his father Colin. The name comes from Egyptian myth. The temple of Amon-Ra is said to have kept the first monoculture vineyard, and Rameses III listed 513 vineyards belonging to it. The Eye of Horus on the label represents the six senses.

**The vineyard.** The vines are 50 to 130 years old, harvested at about one tonne per hectare, and aged 14 months in 100% new oak. That oak is 95% French and 5% American.

**What the critics say for 2012.** The scores are high but more spread out than for the other two wines.
- **Wine Advocate:** Lisa Perrotti-Brown gave 97+ in February 2014. Her notes describe a very dark wine with blackcurrant, licorice, spice and a savoury edge. One UK merchant instead reports 96 points from her, so there is a small conflict. The 97+ appears in several retailers' listings, including K&L.
- **Vinous:** 94 points (August 2013).
- **Wine Spectator:** 93 points.
- **James Halliday:** A gold medal in July 2014. He said the wine carries its alcohol well and should reach its peak after its 21st birthday, so around 2033. K&L's page doesn't show a numeric score.
- **James Suckling:** 89 points, because he found the oak a little heavy.
- The CellarTracker community score of 93.5 is from your list. I did not retrieve that page.

**Practical note.** The Wine Advocate's drinking window ran 2015 to 2025, so the wine has reached it. Halliday's longer view means you can keep it a few more years. Amon-Ra is unfiltered, so decant it for sediment and for air, about an hour. Grilled beef, braised lamb or a hard aged cheese will suit it. A retailer lists beef, hard cheese and duck for the 2019 vintage.

**An aside on the soil.** Ebenezer's well-drained sandy clay loams sit over a solid limestone pan, which encourages deep roots. Warm temperatures, low rainfall and low humidity also help concentrate the fruit. The Barossa is one of the last bastions of old vines largely untouched by phylloxera.

**From the history books**
- About 12th century BC: Rameses III's records of the Amun temple's vineyards, the namesake story. [Ramesses III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Ramesses+III&go=Go)
- 1888: the Glaetzer family arrives in the Barossa. [Barossa Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Barossa+Valley+wine+region&go=Go)
- 1995: Glaetzer Wines founded by Ben Glaetzer. [Phylloxera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Phylloxera&go=Go)
